strategy_objective_guidance:
- The evaluator wrapper (`evaluate` in `evaluator.py`, invoked identically for stage1/2/3) is not fully visible here; all three stages run the same scoring, so there is no stage-specific objective shift. The scored quantity is the total data-transfer cost of the broadcast plan produced by `search_algorithm(src, dsts, G, num_partitions)` — i.e., the sum of edge/link costs (possibly time-weighted or congestion-weighted by the underlying `BroadCastTopology` cost model) over all transfers executed to deliver data from `src` to every node in `dsts`.
- What is rewarded: lower total transfer cost. The problem statement names three cost-reduction mechanisms that the hidden cost function almost certainly encodes: (a) eliminating redundant transfers (reuse an already-delivered intermediate node instead of re-sending from `src`), (b) load balance / overlap across parallel network paths (models where simultaneous transfers on a shared link cost more, or where the objective is makespan-like), and (c) exploitation of the multi-network topology `G` (transit via cheap cross-network gateways rather than direct expensive links).
- Hard validity constraints (implicit): every destination in `dsts` must receive the data (feasibility dominates score), and the returned plan must be expressible with the expected `BroadCastTopology` / `make_nx_graph` interfaces — signature compatibility is a validity gate, not a scored term.
- Complete input is available at once: `src`, `dsts`, `G`, and `num_partitions` are all passed to the function before any decision is made. This permits fully offline/batch, non-causal, global optimization (e.g., computing a Steiner tree, min-cost flow, or partitioned multicast over the whole graph). Do not restrict search to greedy streaming heuristics.
- `num_partitions` suggests the cost model may reward splitting the data into chunks routed on parallel paths (increases overlap/balance, decreases per-link cost or makespan) — but partitioning can also add per-transfer overhead, so chunk count trades off against per-chunk fixed cost. That tradeoff (redundancy elimination vs. parallelism overhead) is the main opposing pair. The largest remaining lever is typically routing through shared intermediate aggregation points (an approximation to the minimum Steiner tree), since naive unicast-to-each-dst duplicates transfers.
- Terms not rewarded: code readability, runtime of `search_algorithm` itself (unless the evaluator times it — assume generous limits and prioritize solution quality), and any property of the plan other than its measured transfer cost.
strategy_diverge_guidance:
- Steiner-tree / multicast-tree approach: build one shared delivery tree from `src` covering `dsts` plus relays, minimizing summed edge cost. `networkx.algorithms.approximation.steinertree.steiner_tree` (exact for small graphs, 2-approx otherwise); if `G` is a `MultiGraph` of networks, collapse with `nx.Graph` weights first via `make_nx_graph`. Directly targets the redundancy-elimination mechanism.
- Min-cost-flow / multi-commodity approach: model each partition as a commodity with unit demand per destination; solve a min-cost flow with `scipy.sparse.csgraph` or `networkx.algorithms.flow.min_cost_flow` / `nx.network_simplex` on a suitably constructed flow network. Captures load balance when link cost is convex in usage; naturally handles `num_partitions` as parallel unit flows.
- Shortest-path-overlay / relay-assignment approach: run `nx.multi_source_dijkstra` or all-pairs `nx.shortest_path` (`scipy.sparse.csgraph.dijkstra`) and then solve the small assignment problem of which relay/egress node serves each destination (choose relays at network boundaries to get cheap cross-network hops). Good when cross-network gateways dominate cost.
- Partition-and-parallelize approach: split data into `num_partitions` chunks, compute k edge-disjoint or near-disjoint cheap paths with `nx.edge_disjoint_paths` / Suurballe-style (`nx.shortest_simple_paths` enumeration) so chunks traverse different links simultaneously — rewards overlap if the cost model prices congestion or transfer wall-clock.
- Makespan/overlap-aware scheduling approach: if cost includes a time term, formulate as a min-makespan schedule over link capacities — a greedy list-scheduling over candidate trees, or `scipy.optimize.linprog` / `scipy.optimize.milp` on a linearized multicast LP over path variables.
strategy_refine_guidance:
- Steiner tree refinement: tune the terminal set — allow using `dsts ∪ high-degree junction nodes ∪ network-gateway nodes` as candidate relays, then prune leaves; iterate terminal pruning until cost stops dropping.
- Partition count sweep: measure cost as a function of chunk granularity (1 … `num_partitions` … finer) on the evaluator feedback signal and pick the cost-minimizing granularity; if per-transfer fixed cost exists there is an interior optimum.
- Path overlap control: enumerate several candidate shortest paths per destination (`nx.shortest_simple_paths`, `nx.shortest_path(G, weight=...)` with perturbed weights) and greedily assign destinations to paths to minimize marginal shared-link load (a local-search / simulated-annealing pass with `numpy.random`).

strategies.title: [steiner-tree] Shared-multicast Steiner tree replacing per-dst unicast Dijkstra
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: steiner-tree-multicast
Replacement scope: Replace the body of `search_algorithm` (the per-destination Dijkstra loop) with a Steiner-tree construction; keep `BroadCastTopology`, `make_nx_graph`, and helper signatures unchanged.
Compute budget: One `nx.algorithms.approximation.steinertree.steiner_tree` call on an undirected symmetrized cost graph (2-approx, polynomial); plus one Dijkstra per unreachable dst as fallback. No iterative restarts. Evaluation-time effect negligible (single approximation call).
Gain mechanism: The incumbent sends each partition of the data from `src` along an independent shortest path per dst, duplicating transfers on shared links (e.g., a common egress link carries the data N×dsts×partitions times). A Steiner tree over terminals {src} ∪ dsts delivers data once per tree edge, directly eliminating the redundancy term in the cost model. This is a genuinely new degree of freedom the incumbent structurally cannot realize: shared relay/aggregation nodes and shared prefixes.
Plan: (1) Copy G to undirected graph U where edge weight = min of the two directed costs (use directed cost if reverse missing). (2) Ensure all dst nodes exist; terminals = {src} ∪ {d in dsts if d != src and d in U}. (3) T = steiner_tree(U, terminals, weight="cost"). (4) Orient T from src via BFS; for each dst, the unique tree path src→dst is its delivery path. (5) For each dst and each partition j in range(num_partitions), append each consecutive edge (s,t) of the tree path as `[s, t, G[s][t] if G.has_edge(s,t) else G[t][s]]` via `append_dst_partition_path`. (6) Fallback: any dst not in T (unreachable) gets plain Dijkstra path in h as the incumbent does; if no path exists, skip gracefully. Validity preserved: every reachable dst receives a complete src→dst path per partition, and the returned object is a valid `BroadCastTopology`.
Expected-gain check: The incumbent's cost is at most (num_dsts × num_partitions) × shortest-path cost; the Steiner tree's edge cost is at most 2× the optimal multicast cost, strictly below the incumbent whenever two dst paths share any link — a falsifiable threshold is total_cost < 1035.14 on the same 5 configs.

strategies.title: [partition-disjoint-paths] Per-partition edge-disjoint path assignment for load
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: partition-disjoint-multirouting
Replacement scope: Replace the per-dst single-path loop in `search_algorithm`; keep partition appending interface and all class definitions unchanged.
Compute budget: For each dst, enumerate up to num_partitions + 2 shortest simple paths (capped, via `nx.shortest_simple_paths` with a hard cap of ~50 examined paths) and greedily assign partitions. Bounded, no restarts.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent routes all num_partitions chunks of a dst over the identical cheapest path, concentrating load on one link set. If the hidden cost model prices congestion or time (makespan-like term), spreading partitions across the k cheapest near-disjoint paths reduces per-link simultaneous flow. This is a new degree of freedom (partition→path assignment) absent from the incumbent.
Plan: (1) Build h as the incumbent does (remove in-edges of src, self-loops). (2) For each dst: enumerate shortest simple paths in nondecreasing cost; greedily build a pool of up to num_partitions paths, accepting a path only if it shares fewer than half its edges with any already-accepted path (cost cap: skip paths whose cost exceeds 1.3× the optimum). (3) Assign partition j to pool path j mod len(pool); if the pool has one path, all partitions share it (degrades to incumbent behavior). (4) Append full edge lists per partition via `append_dst_partition_path`. (5) Unreachable dsts skipped gracefully; every reachable dst gets a complete path per partition — validity preserved.
Expected-gain check: If the evaluator's cost includes any congestion/time weighting, per-dst link load drops from num_partitions flows to ~1 flow per link; falsifiable threshold: total_cost < 1035.14, and if it scores worse, that falsifies the congestion term and the incumbent remains fallback.

strategies.title: [relay-overlay] Two-hop relay assignment over cheapest egress nodes
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: relay-overlay-assignment
Replacement scope: Replace the routing logic inside `search_algorithm` with a two-segment relay construction; classes and interfaces unchanged.
Compute budget: One all-pairs Dijkstra (or per-candidate single-source Dijkstras limited to candidate relays: src plus up to ~20 lowest-cost-hub nodes chosen by min total incident cost), then a small min-assignment over dsts×relays. No iterative optimization.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's single shortest path cannot exploit the multi-network topology's cheap gateways when the direct cheapest path is expensive; a two-hop construction src→relay→dst lets each dst enter its network through the cheapest egress point, a structurally different contact topology (star-of-stars) versus per-dst paths.
Plan: (1) Compute d_src(v) = Dijkstra cost from src to all v in h. (2) Candidate relays R = {src} ∪ top-20 nodes ranked by sum of incident edge costs (cheap hubs), restricted to nodes with d_src finite. (5) Append full two-segment edge lists per partition; skip unreachable dsts; complete paths guaranteed for all reachable dsts — validity preserved.
Expected-gain check: Because the construction's feasible set strictly contains the incumbent's (relay = src recovers shortest path), the computed minimum is ≤ the incumbent's per-dst path cost with equality only when direct is optimal; falsifiable threshold: total_cost ≤ 1035.14 with strict improvement expected on any config where a cheap hub lies off the direct path.

strategies.title: [directed-steiner] Directed Takahashi multicast tree replacing the symmetrized u
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: directed-steiner
Replacement scope: Replace the graph-symmetrization + `steiner_tree` block inside `search_algorithm` (the `U = nx.Graph()` construction, the `steiner_tree(U, ...)` call, and the BFS orientation) with a directed incremental-terminal construction; keep the `record`/fallback machinery unchanged.
Compute budget: One pass of the directed Takahashi heuristic: for each dst (ordered by ascending directed Dijkstra distance from src, ≤ |dsts| shortest-path solves), one Dijkstra from that dst over the reverse graph — O(|dsts| · Dijkstra). No iterations beyond that; expected evaluation-time effect negligible (graphs are small region graphs).
Gain mechanism: The incumbent symmetrizes edges with `min(cost(s,t), cost(t,s))` and then records the edge with `edge_data(s,t)` falling back to `G[t][s]` — so a tree hop may be recorded against a reverse directed edge whose true cost in `G` is far higher than the symmetrized weight the Steiner solver optimized. The evaluator charges actual recorded edge costs, so the incumbent's internal objective diverges from the scored cost on every asymmetric pair. The new degree of freedom is directionality: build the tree with the directed shortest-path heuristic (start tree = {src}; repeatedly attach the nearest uncovered terminal to the existing tree using Dijkstra on the reverse graph from the terminal to the tree node set, then record the directed path). Every recorded edge then has its true directed cost, and the internal objective monotonically matches the scored cost. Keep the undirected Steiner result as an incumbent fallback and emit whichever plan has lower internally-computed total directed cost (sum over recorded edges × num_partitions), so the plan is never worse than the current parent.
Expected-gain check: whenever any edge (s,t) used by the current tree satisfies cost_G(t,s) < cost_G(s,t) (i.e., the symmetrized weight underestimates the recorded directed cost), the incumbent overpays relative to its own optimized objective; the directed construction removes that exact overpayment, so the predicted total_cost is strictly below 741.40 on any config with asymmetric pairs, and equal otherwise via the fallback.

strategies.title: [marginal-cost-multicommodity] Per-partition marginal-cost path assignment with
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: marginal-cost-multicommodity
Replacement scope: Replace the entire path-assignment logic in `search_algorithm` (both the Steiner block and the per-dst Dijkstra fallback) with a greedy marginal-cost multicommodity assignment; `BroadCastTopology`, `record`-style edge emission, and fallbacks stay.
Compute budget: For each (dst, partition) pair (≤ |dsts| · num_partitions, e.g. ≤ 5·4=20 commodities), enumerate at most K=8 candidate paths via `nx.shortest_simple_paths` on a priced copy of G, and run at most 3 greedy passes; hard cap 20·8 shortest-path enumerations. Evaluation-time effect: small (seconds).
Gain mechanism: The incumbent sends all num_partitions copies of each dst down the identical tree path, quadrupling the load on every shared link; if the evaluator's cost model prices congestion or per-link volume (the stated "balance load across networks" mechanism), this is the dominant remaining cost. New degree of freedom: per-partition routing. Maintain a mutable price map p(e) = base_cost(e) · (1 + λ·load(e)/throughput(e)) where load(e) counts partitions already assigned through e; for each commodity in a fixed order, pick the cheapest candidate path under current prices and commit it. This spreads partitions across parallel near-equal-cost routes (multi-network topology gives several such routes between region pairs) while keeping each single path a true directed shortest path, preserving feasibility (every dst gets all partitions). Fallback: if any dst has only one feasible path, all its partitions reuse it (identical to incumbent behavior there).
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is partition-diverse routing under congestion pricing, which the incumbent structurally cannot express (all partitions share one path); the falsifiable threshold is total_cost < 741.40 on at least one of the 5 successful configs, with a guaranteed-no-regression guard comparing summed base edge costs against the incumbent plan's before emission.

strategies.title: [steiner-local-search] Edge-swap / subtree-prune local search polishing the incu
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: steiner-local-search
Replacement scope: Insert a bounded local-search phase between the Steiner tree construction and the `record` emission inside `search_algorithm`; the tree construction, fallbacks, and all interfaces are untouched.
Compute budget: At most 2 full sweeps; each sweep tries (a) removing each non-terminal degree-1/degree-2 tree node (≤ |V| moves) and (b) re-attaching each dst's subtree at each of its ≤ 3 cheapest alternative one-hop neighbors; hard cap ~200 candidate moves total, each evaluated by O(1) incremental cost delta. No random restarts.
Gain mechanism: The 2-approximation `steiner_tree` output is not locally optimal: it typically contains removable Steiner (relay) nodes whose deletion plus direct reconnection lowers cost, and subtrees attached at suboptimal junction points. The new degree of freedom is post-hoc tree topology: compute the plan's exact scored cost internally (sum of directed edge costs × num_partitions over recorded edges), apply the cheapest improving move (delete relay node and reconnect its neighbors via directed shortest path; or re-root a dst's branch at a cheaper junction), and iterate accept-only-improving. Because moves are gated on strictly positive delta in the same cost the evaluator charges, the emitted plan is never worse than the incumbent's Steiner tree; the gain is the gap between the 2-approximation and its local optimum, which is nonzero whenever any relay node is deletable or any branch junction is improvable.
Expected-gain check: the transformation is a strictly-cost-decreasing local move set evaluated on the exact scored objective, so the predicted total_cost is ≤ 741.40 with strict improvement on any config where the approximation tree contains a deletable relay or suboptimal junction — a directly falsifiable threshold of total_cost < 741.40 while keeping all 5 configs successful.

strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: k-shortest-path-portfolio
Replacement scope: Replace the `build_solution` Steiner-tree construction inside `search_algorithm` (keep the exact `sol_cost` objective, the `record` function, and the Dijkstra fallback untouched); the local-search polish phase can be retained as a final step.
Compute budget: ≤ 8 candidate paths per dst via `nx.shortest_simple_paths` (generator, break after 8), selection sweep ≤ 5 passes over dsts; expected evaluation-time effect negligible (graphs are small region topologies).

strategies.title: ordered attempt [steiner-lp-rounding] Directed-cut Steiner LP relaxation with randomized roundin

Mechanism family: steiner-lp-rounding
Replacement scope: a new standalone construction `lp_round_solution()` inserted as an additional candidate generator feeding the same best-of comparator in `search_algorithm` (alongside the two `build_solution` modes); recording and fallbacks unchanged.
Compute budget: ≤20 LP solves (one per random perturbation) via `scipy.optimize.linprog` (HiGHS) on the bidirected cut LP with ≤ 2|dsts|·|V| constraints — each solve is small (tens of nodes, hundreds of edges); plus ≤200 rounding samples total. strategies.title: [perturbation-multistart-steiner] Weight-perturbed exact Steiner multistart seed

strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: tree-tail-reattachment
Replacement scope: Add a new deterministic post-processing phase in `search_algorithm`, executed after `build_solution` returns `best_map` and before `record` is called; it rewrites `paths_map` in place.
Compute budget: One `nx.single_source_dijkstra` on the reversed graph per tree node with out-edges... concretely: for each dst, one cached `nx.shortest_simple_paths`-free Dijkstra from each tree node v to dst (≤ |tree nodes| ≤ |V| Dijkstras per dst, capped at 30 total Dijkstras across the run). It cannot express the hybrid "ride the shared trunk to some node v, then take a fresh cheap directed tail v→dst" unless that exact concatenation happens to be among the 5 enumerated simple paths from src. The new degree of freedom is the *attachment point*: for each dst d and each node v on the current union of used trunk edges, form candidate path = (current best src→v prefix in paths_map, restricted to shared edges) + Dijkstra(v→d, weight=cost), evaluate the full solution with `sol_cost` (which charges shared edges once), and accept greedily per dst, sweeping dsts in decreasing order of their current path cost. strategies.title: [throughput-balanced-multiroute] Partition-level load balancing across parallel
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: throughput-balanced-multiroute
Replacement scope: Replace the `record` phase of `search_algorithm`: instead of writing the same edge sequence into all `num_partitions` slots of each dst, assign each partition a route chosen from a per-dst candidate set so per-edge partition load stays balanced against edge throughput.
Compute budget: Per dst, ≤ 5 candidate routes via `islice(nx.shortest_simple_paths(h, src, dst, weight="cost"), 5)` (already computed in the incumbent; reuse). Assignment is a single greedy pass over partitions×dsts (≤ num_partitions × |dsts| ≤ 24 units) minimizing max per-edge utilization Σpartitions(edge) / throughput(edge). Negligible evaluation-time effect.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent records the identical transfer plan for every partition, so if the evaluator's cost model is congestion- or time-weighted (the `make_nx_graph` schema carries per-edge `throughput` and the task statement explicitly names load balance / overlap across parallel networks as a scored mechanism), sending all partitions over the same links maximizes per-link load. The new degree of freedom is per-partition route differentiation under a load-balance objective: each partition of a dst may take a different one of the 5 cheapest paths; a greedy scheduler distributes partitions so no edge carries more partitions than necessary, using the throughput values already present on every G edge (no fabricated data). Feasibility: every dst still receives all partitions (each partition slot gets a valid src→dst path); every dst in `dsts` is covered exactly as before.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is per-partition route choice under a throughput-load objective — the incumbent sets all partitions identically and cannot reduce any congestion/makespan term; falsifiable threshold: combined_score > 0.001585 on the same 5 configs, with the metric-named fallback guaranteeing no regression below the incumbent if the evaluator prices only per-GB union cost.

strategies.plan:
<STRATEGY_TITLE>[steiner-star-insertion] Relay-star vertex insertion on the incumbent plan</STRATEGY>
Mechanism family: steiner-star-insertion
Replacement scope: The seed-generation phase inside `build_solution` in `search_algorithm` — add a fourth seed (and a post-anneal refinement pass) built by iterative relay-star insertion on the best incumbent path map; do not touch `record`, `sol_cost`, or the fallback Dijkstra logic.
Compute budget: ≤ |V| candidate relays per pass, ≤ 5 insertion passes, each pass evaluating ≤ |V|×|dsts| candidate reroutes with cached src→v and v→dst Dijkstra distances (2 Dijkstra runs per candidate relay via reverse-graph runs, ≤ 2|V| Dijkstras total per pass). Negligible evaluation-time effect (adds at most ~10|V| Dijkstra calls).
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's seeds only contain relays that lie on some src→dst shortest path or Steiner-tree edge; no seed can discover an interior node v whose *star* (ship src→v once, then v→dst_i for a subset of dsts) beats the union cost, because per-dst Dijkstra never routes through v unless it is individually shortest and the Steiner seeds are built on a symmetrized cost that distorts asymmetric edges. The new degree of freedom is the relay node chosen *before* path assignment: for each unused/interior node v, compute d(src,v) + Σ d(v,dst_i) over each dst whose path currently costs more than its v-reroute, accept the v and dst-subset that maximizes exact `sol_cost` reduction (sol_cost already charges shared edges once, so the src→v trunk is automatically free for additional dsts). Iterate until no insertion improves. Feasibility: every candidate path is a real directed path in G, and all proposals pass through the existing best-of-seeds guard, so validity and the incumbent fallback are preserved.
Expected-gain check: the pass is strictly cost-decreasing on the exact scored union objective and terminates at a plan whose cost is ≤ the incumbent's 126.02 avg; if any single relay star exists with positive marginal gain (the seeds provably cannot express one), avg_cost drops below 126.016809 and the score rises above 0.00158457 — falsifiable by rerunning the evaluator and comparing avg_cost.
</STRATEGY>

<STRATEGY_TITLE>[destination-forest-decomposition] Split dsts into 2–4 subgroups, each with its own multicast tree</STRATEGY>
Mechanism family: destination-forest-decomposition
Replacement scope: Replace the single-tree assumption in `build_solution` (and the incumbent's single `pmap` construction) with a forest construction: partition dsts into K ∈ {2,3} groups, build one directed Steiner/Prim arborescence per group from the same src, and select the cheapest forest by exact `sol_cost`.
Compute budget: ≤ 2 grouping methods (greedy k-medoids on all-pairs directed distances, plus agglomerative merge of cheapest shared-prefix groups) × K ∈ {2,3}, each group solved by the existing seed-B directed Prim-Steiner routine; total ≤ 12 group-tree constructions, each bounded by the existing per-group terminal count. Evaluation-time effect: small (each subproblem is smaller than the incumbent's single problem).
Gain mechanism: The incumbent forces all dsts into one shared tree, so a single expensive trunk edge is bought even when only one geographic cluster needs it; with K groups, group A's trunk edge is not forced onto group B, and the union objective still dedups edges used by multiple groups (e.g., the common src egress). Greedy grouping: cluster dsts by pairwise cost d(dst_i, dst_j) (cost of the cheaper direction from the tree-cost perspective via the already-symmetrized U), then evaluate all forests and keep the best by `sol_cost`; the best single tree (K=1) is the current incumbent, so the forest can only match-or-beat it by construction. Feasibility: each group's paths come from the existing validated tree/path machinery and are recorded through the same `record` helper, preserving path continuity and coverage of every dst.
Expected-gain check: a plan that is never worse than the incumbent by construction plus a new reachable topology (multi-trunk forest) that the single-tree incumbent cannot express; falsifiable threshold — any config where the greedy K=2 forest's `sol_cost` is strictly below the K=1 tree's implies avg_cost < 126.016809 and combined_score > 0.00158457.
</STRATEGY>

<STRATEGY_TITLE>[fixed-charge-flow-inflation] Iteratively reweighted min-cost-flow with share-amortized edge prices</STRATEGY>
Mechanism family: fixed-charge-flow-inflation
Replacement scope: Replace the seed-generation stage of `build_solution` (the three seeds A/B/C) with a fixed-charge-flow seed: build an auxiliary digraph where each dst is a sink with unit demand per partition (num_partitions × |dsts| unit commodities), solve min-cost flow with `nx.network_simplex`, then re-solve with each edge's price deflated by its current flow share (cost_e ← c_e / max(1, ⌊f_e⌋)), iterating to a fixed point; the resulting edge-usage map is decomposed into per-dst directed paths that seed the existing annealer unchanged.
Compute budget: ≤ 6 network_simplex solves on a graph with |V|+|E|+|dsts| nodes and unit capacities, each solve bounded by network simplex on a graph of ≤ a few hundred nodes; evaluation-time effect is a few extra LP solves, well under a second.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's per-dst path construction charges each dst its full path cost internally until the union objective dedups at evaluation time, so no seed *searches* for edges worth sharing across multiple destinations — sharing only emerges by luck of overlapping shortest paths. The flow-with-inflation loop makes the buy-once economics explicit: an edge carrying k commodities effectively costs c_e/k per commodity in the LP, so the simplex actively concentrates commodities onto shared cheap trunks, producing a seed with deliberately overlapping paths (a solution to the fixed-charge multicast relaxation that none of seeds A/B/C can express). Paths extracted from positive-flow edges are real directed paths in G, and the incumbent best-of-seeds guard plus fallback Dijkstra coverage preserve validity and the current incumbent as a floor.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is a share-amortized price in the routing solver, which the incumbent's per-dst shortest-path seeds cannot realize; falsifiable threshold — if the fixed-point flow seed's `sol_cost` on any config is strictly below the best incumbent seed's (union cost < 630.08 total / < 126.02 avg), combined_score rises above 0.00158457; otherwise the family is dead.
</STRATEGY>
